subject: green shore crab
title: A Barnacle Turns Male Crabs Into Mothers for Its Own Eggs

scenes.text: This male crab is raising babies. None of them are his.
A barnacle larva found a soft joint in his shell and injected itself inside. No shell. Just its body.
It grew roots through his whole body and destroyed his reproductive organs.
Then it rewired his hormones. His abdomen widened like a female's. He started doing female mating dances.
A sac bulged out where a female carries eggs. He grooms it, guards it, and fans its larvae into the sea.
He can never molt or grow again. He's a nursery now. On some shores, half the crabs are.

description:
The parasitic barnacle Sacculina injects itself into a green shore crab through a joint, spreads root-like tendrils through its body and destroys its reproductive organs.
In males it changes the hormones: the abdomen widens and flattens like a female's, the crab performs female mating dances, and it grooms and releases the barnacle's larvae as if they were its own eggs. The crab can no longer molt. In some green crab populations about 50 percent are infected.
Is this worse than the zombie ant fungus? Comment below.
first_comment: Sacculina is a real barnacle, a cousin of the ones stuck to rocks, that gave up its shell entirely. Eating an infected crab is harmless to humans. Which body-snatching parasite should we do next?
